draft.title: Retelling and reimagining stories
card: A retelling takes an older story and tells it again in a new way. The writer may change the setting, the time, the form or who tells it.
a writer retells a story to challenge its values, such as who is treated as the hero or whose actions are excused.
a writer moves a story into a new time or place so a new audience can connect with it.

a writer tells the story through a character who was silent or barely heard in the original. Comparing the original with a retelling shows what each version values, by what was kept, changed or added.
draft.remember: A retelling changes an older story for a reason, and the changes show what each version values.

a.q: A novel retells a fairy tale from the point of view of the stepmother, who barely spoke in the original. What is the writer mainly doing?
opts: Giving a voice to a character who was silent
Updating the story for a modern audience
Copying the original story word for word
Changing the story's form from prose to film
a.why: The writer tells the story through a character who had almost no voice in the original. Updating is a tempting answer, but the card ties updating to a new time or place, and nothing here says the setting has changed.
a.clue: Whose point of view is new?

b.q: An original tale has a prince rescue a village from a wolf. Mia writes a version where the villagers tame the wolf and the prince is ignored. What does comparing the two versions best show?
opts: The original values a lone rescuer, Mia's values community
The original values kindness, Mia's values bravery
Both versions value the same things in the same way
Mia's version is better because it has a new ending
b.why: The original rewards one hero who acts alone. Mia's version removes him and credits the villagers, so the change shows a different value. A new ending alone does not show which version is better, as comparing shows what each values.
b.clue: Look at who solves the problem in each version.

a.best: Giving a voice to a character who was silent

proposal.title: Retelling and reimagining stories
card: A retelling takes an older story and tells it again in a new way. The writer may change the setting, the time, the form or who tells it.
Some writers retell a story to question its values, such as who is treated as the hero. Others update it, moving it to a new time or place so a new audience can connect with it.
A retelling can also give a voice to a character who was silent or barely heard in the original, by telling the story through them.
Whatever the purpose, comparing the original with a retelling shows what each version values, through what was kept, changed or added.
proposal.remember: A retelling changes an older story for a reason, and the changes show what each version values.
